question: What will be the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for August 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for August 2026 (FRED series PAYEMS, diff). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
# August 2026 nonfarm payrolls (first print): research brief

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the first published August 2026 value of the BLS Employment Situation report (FRED PAYEMS, monthly difference). The release is expected Friday 2026-09-04 at 8:30 ET, which fits the stated resolution time.
- 2026-08-07: The latest official print is July 2026 at **-23K**. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/little-change-in-nonfarm-payroll-employment-in-july-2026.htm), [BLS release archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072026.htm)
- I could not open the BLS and FRED pages directly because the proxy refused the connection. All figures below come from search summaries of news coverage.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The August figure is unpublished as of 2026-08-28.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-27: Initial jobless claims for the week ending Aug 22 were 203K, down from 207K. PNC describes the labor market as stable, with no sign of rising layoffs. [PNC](https://www.pnc.com/content/dam/pnc-com/pdf/aboutpnc/EconomicReports/EconomicUpdates/2026/PNC_Economics_Research_Claims_27_August_2026.pdf)
- 2026-08-25: The Conference Board index slipped to 89.4 from 90.2. The "jobs plentiful minus hard to get" gap rose for the first time in three months, coming off July's lowest level in more than five years. The Expectations Index fell 5.8 points, with consumers more pessimistic about jobs. [Kitco/Reuters](https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-08-25/us-consumer-confidence-falls-august-conference-board-says), [Anews](https://www.anews.com.tr/americas/2026/08/25/us-consumer-confidence-unexpectedly-falls-in-august)
- Mid-August 2026: In ADP's weekly NER Pulse (4-week average, private sector), the week ending Aug 8 showed +11,750 jobs per week, up from 9,500 in the week ending Aug 1. The week ending Jul 25 had been 8,250, the lowest since January, and June peaked near 30,750. [Cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/adp-weekly-jobs-pulse-august-8-2026/), [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/4020506/adp-national-employment-report-preliminary-estimate-for-august-8-2026)
- 2026-08-20: Claims for the week ending Aug 15 were 206K against 210K expected. The 4-week average was about 204K. [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/us-initial-jobless-claims-206k-vs-210k-expected/)
- 2026-08-07: Details of the July report:
  - Payrolls fell 23K against a consensus of roughly 80-95K. The Reuters poll range was 10K to 140K.
  - Revisions: May was cut from 129K to 63K and June from 57K to 20K, a combined -103K.
  - Government jobs fell 53K, all in local government education, which suggests a seasonal-adjustment or education quirk. Leisure and hospitality fell 40K and retail fell 19K.
  - Participation fell to 61.4%, a more than five-year low. Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% (3.2% year on year).
  - Sources: [First Trust](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/8/7/nonfarm-payrolls-declined-23,000-in-july), [Haver](https://www.haver.com/articles/u-s-payroll-employment-unexpectedly-declined-in-july), [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/us-jobs-fall-unexpectedly-in-july-as-earlier-payrolls-revised-lower-126080702115_1.html)
- 2026-08-07: July's ADP monthly private payrolls were about +44K. [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/08/07/july-2026-jobs-report-unexpected-turbulence/)

## 4. Base rates
- **First prints in 2026:**
  - Jan +130K [JEC](https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/vendor/_accounts/JEC-R/employment/national/Monthly%20Employment%20Update%20%28PDF%29.pdf)
  - Feb -92K and Mar +178K [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/non-farm-payrolls)
  - Apr: I could not find a reliable first print.
  - May +129K, Jun +57K, Jul -23K
- **Averages:** As of 2026-08-07, the 3-month average was about +20K, down from 77K in the three months through June. One source puts the prior 12-month average at about 34K per month. [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/us-jobs-fall-unexpectedly-in-july-as-earlier-payrolls-revised-lower-126080702115_1.html)
- **Volatility:** First prints swung by roughly ±100-150K month to month in 2026, and two of seven were negative. The July miss against consensus was about 100K. Big misses in both directions have been common this year.
- **Possible bounce-back:** If the July government-education drop was a seasonal artifact, August could rebound partly in that category. This is my inference, not a sourced claim.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no consensus figure clearly dated on or before 2026-08-28. Consensus is usually set the week of the release, after this question closes.
- Kalshi does list a KXPAYROLLS-26AUG market. The only price snapshots I found are on a mirror site that labels them as computed in June 2026, so they are stale: about 85% for above 0, 47% for above 70K, and about 5% for above 100K. Do not treat these as current. [simplefunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXPAYROLLS-26AUG-T0)
- I found no dated Polymarket or Manifold price for August from before Aug 28. A Manifold payroll market exists. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/will-us-nonfarm-payroll-employment)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Tuesday 2026-09-01: ADP weekly NER Pulse (if published that week) and the JOLTS July report (typical timing).
- Wednesday 2026-09-02: ADP monthly National Employment Report for August (typical timing).
- Thursday 2026-09-03: Weekly jobless claims for the week ending Aug 29, plus the ISM services employment index around then.
- Friday 2026-09-04, 8:30 ET: BLS Employment Situation for August. This release resolves the question, and it will also revise June and July.
- Note: forecasts close 2026-08-28 18:00 UTC, before all of these.
